title: An observability agent gains database access
question: A supplier component gains read permission to a sensitive store. Which trust edge changed, and what architecture vulnerability assumptions need reassessment?
scenario: A managed observability agent previously read application health metrics only. An upgrade grants its supplier-maintained service identity read access to the customer-record database so it can enrich traces. The supplier, update path, and support process are unchanged, but the component can now cross a sensitive data boundary.
focalRelation: Supply-chain facts about supplier control, updates, support, and assurance inform architecture analysis when a component gains a new permission edge. The permission change creates exposure; it is not evidence that compromise occurred.

nodes.label: Supplier-controlled component
nodes.detail: The vendor maintains agent code, release signing, support access, and updates; those dependencies define the supply-chain subject under review.

nodes.label: Before: metrics read
nodes.detail: The agent could read low-sensitivity health metrics and send them to the approved observability service.

nodes.label: After: customer-record read
nodes.detail: The service identity can now query sensitive customer records, crossing a data trust boundary with a new least-privilege and exfiltration consequence.

nodes.label: Assumptions to reopen
nodes.detail: Reassess data need, permission scope, query controls, egress, update provenance, support access, monitoring, revocation, and failure containment.

nodes.label: Approve, reduce, isolate, or reject
nodes.detail: An accountable architecture and supplier-risk review chooses a bounded control response before the permission reaches production.

states.title: Supplier dependency, limited reach
states.caption: The original review covered a component that read metrics, not customer records.

states.title: One permission edge changes
states.caption: The component is not declared compromised; its possible reach and failure consequence changed.

states.title: Reopen the assumptions attached to that edge
states.caption: Assess necessity, data scope, identity, update provenance, egress, observability, support paths, and revocation.

states.title: Choose a bounded architecture response
states.caption: Reduce or isolate the permission unless evidence supports the requirement and its controls.

variants.label: Support path added
variants.changedFact: The component’s data permission stays limited, but the supplier receives a standing remote support path to its host.

states.title: The changed edge is administrative
states.caption: Reassess the supplier’s human access, authentication, session recording, approval, segmentation, and revocation rather than database query scope.

states.title: Constrain the support boundary
states.caption: Prefer time-bounded approved access with attributable evidence over an unrestricted standing path.

prediction.prompt: What changed in the architecture when the upgrade gained customer-record read access?

options.label: The supplier identity now crosses a sensitive-data boundary
options.feedback: Correct. The new edge changes trust-boundary exposure and the consequence of supplier, update, credential, or component failure.

options.label: The permission change confirms that the supplier is compromised
options.feedback: Permission creates possible reach, not proof of malicious use or compromise.

options.label: The earlier approval covers every permission later granted to the agent
options.feedback: The prior approval covered a different access scope and cannot silently authorize a new sensitive edge.

prediction.hint: Compare the component’s possible data reach before and after without inventing an event.

transfer.prompt: If the changed fact is a standing remote support path instead, what should the reassessment center on?

options.label: Database filtering alone removes the remote-support trust path
options.feedback: Row filtering does not address a new host administration path.

options.label: Remote support adds an administered path across the trust boundary
options.feedback: Correct. The trust edge now concerns supplier support authority rather than database query permission.

options.label: Unchanged data permissions make the remote-support path exempt from review
options.feedback: A new privileged support path changes architecture trust even when application data permissions remain stable.

transfer.hint: Name the actor and authority introduced by the new edge.

retry.prompt: A routine agent update requests no new permission, but its signature no longer chains to the approved supplier key. What controls the deployment decision?

options.label: Approve it because the supplier and requested permissions are unchanged
options.feedback: An unchanged supplier name and permission set do not establish the provenance or integrity of the new artifact.

options.label: Deploy it first and use runtime monitoring to decide whether it was authentic
options.feedback: Monitoring can observe behavior after execution; it cannot replace provenance verification before trusted deployment.

options.label: Quarantine the update until its signing path and approved provenance are verified
options.feedback: Correct. The changed artifact must be bound to an approved supplier update path before it enters the architecture.

retry.hint: Treat artifact provenance as a trust claim separate from the supplier name and requested permission.

takeaway: Supplier dependencies alter architecture when their code, identities, updates, or support paths gain new reach. Reassess the changed edge and its failure consequences without treating possible access as an observed compromise.
assumptions: The upgrade’s permission request is known before production deployment.
The supplier component has not been observed abusing the access.
The prior approval and current architecture are available for before/after comparison.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The before/after case teaches the assigned SCRM-to-architecture direction by isolating the changed trust edge, its assumptions, and a bounded approval decision without simulating compromise.

learningJob.plainExplanation: granting the supplier-managed agent customer-record access creates a new sensitive trust edge; it increases possible reach and failure impact without proving compromise. Reassess necessity, scope, update/support authority, egress, monitoring, and revocation before approving a bounded response.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The revealed visual adds a before/after path and collects the assumptions attached to the new edge, but the unrevealed opening shows only the supplier subject and previous metrics access, so the visual prediction lacks the changed endpoint it asks the learner to reason about.
